newsitem.title: FRANCE: France, Italy say determined to join EMU on time.
newsitem.headline: France, Italy say determined to join EMU on time.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac and Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Thursday they were determined that their countries should join European economic and monetary union on schedule, the French leader's office said.

A French spokesman said Chirac telephoned Prodi to discuss economic and monetary questions and NATO issues. "Each man reaffirmed his determination to see his country join the euro at the planned date (January 1999)," he said.

French sources said Chirac had above all sought to reassure Prodi in the half-hour conversation that France and Germany were not discussing any deal behind Rome's back to delay Italian membership of the planned single European currency.

Despite open reluctance in German banking circles, Paris and Bonn have stuck to the line that each country should do its best to meet the criteria for monetary union and a decision should be taken early next year on the basis of 1997 data.
Chirac's office said the two leaders had also stressed the need for European Union countries to coordinate their economic policies to fight unemployment.
They also discussed the reform and enlargement of NATO, in which France is pressing the United States to yield the alliance's Naples-based Southern Command to a European.
